records.source: בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ־לִ֥י לְעָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: At the time the that, declares Yahweh, I will be for God to all [the] clans of Israel, and they, they will be to me for a people.
pieces: At that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I will be God to every clan of Israel, \q and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

L.1: At that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I will be God to all the clans of Israel, \q and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

R.1: When that time comes, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I will be God to every family in Israel, \q and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

decisions.choice: at that time: the time just announced at the end of chapter 30, when the LORD's purpose is carried out
decisions.reason: "At that time" points back to "the last days" of 30:24. Chapters 30 and 31 are one collection of promises that God told Jeremiah to write in a book (30:2), so this verse both closes the warning of 30:23-24 and opens the promises of chapter 31.

decisions.choice: I will be God to them, and they will be my people: the covenant promise
decisions.reason: These words sum up the covenant God made with Israel (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Jeremiah repeats them for the future (24:7; 30:22), and they return in the new covenant of 31:33.

decisions.choice: all the clans of Israel: the whole people, both the northern tribes and Judah
decisions.reason: The clans are the family groups that made up the tribes. "All" of them includes the northern kingdom, long scattered by Assyria, as the following verses about Ephraim and Samaria show (31:5-6, 9, 18-20).

decisions.choice: families
decisions.reason: Readable says "families" for the clans, a word young readers know; Literal and Balanced keep "clans".

records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מָצָ֥א חֵן֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר עַ֖ם שְׂרִ֣ידֵי חָ֑רֶב הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: found favor in the wilderness [the] people of [the] survivors of [the] sword; going to give rest to him, Israel.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q The people who escaped the sword found favor in the wilderness \q as Israel went in search of rest.

L.2: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q The people, survivors of the sword, found favor in the wilderness; \q [when] Israel went to find rest.

R.2: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q The people who lived through the war found kindness in the desert, \q when Israel went looking for rest.

decisions.choice: found favor in the wilderness: God's kindness to Israel in the desert after the exodus, now promised again
decisions.reason: The wilderness recalls the forty years after Israel left Egypt, when God cared for the people (2:2). The survivors of the sword were those who escaped Pharaoh's army then; the words also fit the survivors of the Assyrian and Babylonian wars, who will meet God's favor on a second journey home. The verbs are in the past, but here they describe a pattern the coming rescue will repeat.

decisions.choice: going to find rest, Israel: Israel's journey toward rest in the land
alternatives: when I went to give Israel rest
I will go to give Israel rest
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short: "going, to give him rest, Israel". It may mean that Israel went to find rest (the promised land, Deuteronomy 12:9), or that God went to give Israel rest (Exodus 33:14; Numbers 10:33). The sense is the same journey from the wilderness to rest, but who goes is uncertain.

decisions.choice: favor: kindness shown freely by one in power
decisions.reason: The word means the favor someone finds in the eyes of a stronger person (Genesis 6:8; Exodus 33:12-17). Here it is God's undeserved kindness to his people.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD: (Literal); The LORD says this: (Balanced); This is what the LORD says: (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one wording for this formula throughout the prophets. As in Isaiah, God's words in the oracles of this chapter take no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: lived through the war ... kindness ... desert
decisions.reason: Readable says "lived through the war" for survivors of the sword and "desert" for the wilderness, and "kindness" for favor.

records.heading: Loved with an everlasting love

records.source: מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י וְאַהֲבַ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ עַל־כֵּ֖ן מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ חָֽסֶד׃
records.gloss: From far away Yahweh appeared to me; and [with] a love of perpetuity I have loved you; therefore I have drawn out to you loyal love.
pieces: From far away {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to me: \q I have loved you with an everlasting love, \q so I have kept on showing you loyal love.

L.3: From far away {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to me. \q And with an everlasting love I have loved you; \q therefore I have drawn out loyal love to you.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to me from far away: \q I have loved you with a love that lasts forever, \q so I have kept on showing you faithful love.

decisions.choice: to me: the people (or the prophet) speaks, recalling how God appeared
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "to me". The speaker is probably Israel, pictured as a woman (the "you" of the next line is feminine), telling how God once appeared to her; it could also be the prophet. The Greek translation reads "to him", making it a statement about Israel.

decisions.choice: from far away: from a distance, probably in place (from Zion to the exiles), perhaps also in time (long ago)
decisions.reason: The word usually means far off in space. God reaches the exiles in distant lands (31:10). It can also point back to long ago, to God's first appearing to Israel at the exodus, which suits the wilderness of verse 2.

decisions.choice: I have drawn out loyal love to you: I have kept my loyal love going toward you
alternatives: I have drawn you with loyal love
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw or pull, and with loyal love as its object it means to prolong or keep up that love (Psalm 36:11; 109:12). Another reading takes "loyal love" as the means: "I have drawn you with loyal love", as with cords of love (Hosea 11:4). Either way, the everlasting love has never stopped.

decisions.choice: loyal love (Literal, Balanced); faithful love (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for God's covenant faithfulness and love is rendered as in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: a love that lasts forever
decisions.reason: Readable says "a love that lasts forever" for "an everlasting love".

records.source: ע֤וֹד אֶבְנֵךְ֙ וְֽנִבְנֵ֔ית בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֚וֹד תַּעְדִּ֣י תֻפַּ֔יִךְ וְיָצָ֖את בִּמְח֥וֹל מְשַׂחֲקִֽים׃
records.gloss: Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin of Israel; again you will adorn yourself [with] your tambourines, and you will go out in [the] dance of merrymakers.
pieces: Once more I will build you, and you will be rebuilt, \q Virgin Israel; \q once more you will deck yourself with your tambourines \q and go out in the dances of the joyful.

L.4: Again I will build you, and you will be built, \q virgin Israel; \q again you will adorn yourself with your tambourines \q and go out in the dance of those who make merry.

R.4: I will build you again, and you will be rebuilt, \q you people of Israel, pure as a young woman. \q Once again you will pick up your tambourines \q and go out dancing with people who celebrate.

decisions.choice: virgin Israel: the nation pictured as a young unmarried woman
decisions.reason: A city or people is often pictured as a young woman (14:17; 18:13). Here the picture is tender: the people who were unfaithful (18:13) and ruined will be made new, like a young woman with her life before her.

decisions.choice: I will build you: the building promised in Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: Building is one of the words of 1:10 ("to build and to plant"), here applied to the people as a house that God rebuilds. Planting follows in verse 5, and both return in verse 28.

decisions.choice: tambourines and dances: women's celebration of victory and rescue
decisions.reason: Women went out with tambourines and dancing to celebrate deliverance (Exodus 15:20; Judges 11:34; 1 Samuel 18:6). "Adorn yourself" pictures the tambourines as jewelry the young woman puts on again.

decisions.choice: you people of Israel, pure as a young woman ... pick up your tambourines
decisions.reason: Readable explains "virgin Israel" as the people pictured as a pure young woman and says "pick up" for putting the tambourines on like ornaments.

records.source: ע֚וֹד תִּטְּעִ֣י כְרָמִ֔ים בְּהָרֵ֖י שֹֽׁמְר֑וֹן נָטְע֥וּ נֹטְעִ֖ים וְחִלֵּֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Again you will plant vineyards on [the] mountains of Samaria; planters will plant and will treat [them] as common.
pieces: Once more you will plant vineyards \q on the hills of Samaria; \q those who plant them will enjoy their fruit.

L.5: Again you will plant vineyards \q on the mountains of Samaria; \q planters will plant and will enjoy [the fruit].

R.5: You will plant vineyards again \q on the hills of Samaria. \q The people who plant them will eat the grapes.

decisions.choice: the mountains of Samaria: the hill country of the old northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Samaria was the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel, destroyed by Assyria about 722 BC (2 Kings 17:5-6). The promise of vineyards there means that the north, long empty of its people, will be settled again.

decisions.choice: will treat them as common: will eat the fruit freely, after the years when it was forbidden
decisions.reason: The law kept the fruit of new trees from use for three years, gave the fourth year's fruit to God, and let the owner eat it from the fifth year (Leviticus 19:23-25). The verb means to make it ordinary, free for use (Deuteronomy 20:6; 28:30). The promise is that those who plant will live long enough in peace to eat what they planted.

decisions.choice: plant: the planting promised in Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: Planting is the last word of 1:10. The curse of Deuteronomy 28:30, planting a vineyard and not enjoying it, is reversed.

decisions.choice: enjoy [the fruit] (Literal); enjoy their fruit (Balanced); eat the grapes (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that they will make the vineyards common; each level says what that means.

records.source: כִּ֣י יֶשׁ־י֔וֹם קָרְא֥וּ נֹצְרִ֖ים בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃פ
records.gloss: For there is a day [when] watchmen will call out in [the] hill country of Ephraim: Arise, and let us go up [to] Zion, to Yahweh our God.
pieces: For a day is coming when watchmen will call out \q on the hills of Ephraim, \q "Come, let us go up to Zion, \q to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God!"

L.6: For there is a day [when] watchmen will call out \q on the hill country of Ephraim: \q "Arise, and let us go up [to] Zion, \q to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."

R.6: A day is coming when watchmen on the hills of Ephraim will shout, \q "Come, let us go up to Zion \q to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God!"

decisions.choice: watchmen: lookouts posted on the hills
decisions.reason: Watchmen kept guard over fields and towns from high places. Here they call the people to go up to a festival, as pilgrims did at the great feasts (Deuteronomy 16:16; Psalm 122:1).

decisions.choice: Ephraim going up to Zion: the north worshiping again at Jerusalem
decisions.reason: After the kingdom split, the northern king Jeroboam set up his own shrines so that his people would not go up to Jerusalem (1 Kings 12:26-29). The promise is that the people of Ephraim, the heart of the north, will themselves call for the journey to Zion. The divided people will worship the LORD together.

decisions.choice: Come (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "Arise" is a call to set out; "Come" says that in today's English. Literal keeps "Arise".

decisions.choice: to worship the LORD our God
decisions.reason: Readable says why the pilgrims go up to Zion.

records.source: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה רָנּ֤וּ לְיַֽעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְחָ֔ה וְצַהֲל֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם הַשְׁמִ֤יעוּ הַֽלְלוּ֙ וְאִמְר֔וּ הוֹשַׁ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֔ אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: Sing aloud [for] Jacob [with] gladness, and shout for [the] head of the nations; proclaim, praise, and say: Save, Yahweh, your people, the remnant of Israel.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Sing for joy over Jacob, \q shout for the foremost of the nations. \q Make it heard, give praise, and say, \q "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q the remnant of Israel!"

L.7: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Sing aloud with gladness for Jacob, \q and shout for the chief of the nations; \q proclaim, praise, and say, \q "Save, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q the remnant of Israel."

R.7: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Sing with joy for the people of Jacob. \q Shout for the greatest of the nations. \q Tell everyone, praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and say, \q "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q those who are left in Israel!"

decisions.choice: the head of the nations: Israel, the foremost nation
alternatives: at the head (top) of the nations
decisions.reason: "Head" here means first or chief. The phrase names Israel, chosen by God (Amos 6:1; Deuteronomy 28:13). It does not mean shouting on the mountaintops of the nations, though "head" can also mean top.

decisions.choice: Save, LORD, your people: a prayer for rescue
alternatives: The LORD has saved his people (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a plea, "Save!", which the joyful context turns into a cry of praise (compare Psalm 118:25). The Greek translation reads a statement, "The LORD has saved his people".

decisions.choice: the remnant of Israel: those who survive the judgment
decisions.reason: The remnant are the people left after war and exile. The prophets promise that God will save and gather them (23:3; Isaiah 10:20-22; Micah 2:12).

decisions.choice: the LORD addressed with no "O"
decisions.reason: As in the Psalms and Isaiah, the divine name in a direct address has no "O" before it.

decisions.choice: the people of Jacob ... praise the LORD ... those who are left
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jacob is the people descended from him, names the one who is praised, and explains "remnant".

records.source: הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אוֹתָ֜ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֗וֹן וְקִבַּצְתִּים֮ מִיַּרְכְּתֵי־אָרֶץ֒ בָּ֚ם עִוֵּ֣ר וּפִסֵּ֔חַ הָרָ֥ה וְיֹלֶ֖דֶת יַחְדָּ֑ו קָהָ֥ל גָּד֖וֹל יָשׁ֥וּבוּ הֵֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: Here I [am] bringing them from [the] land of [the] north, and I will gather them from [the] farthest parts of [the] earth; among them [the] blind and [the] lame, [the] pregnant and [the one] giving birth together; a great assembly they will return here.
pieces: I am going to bring them out of the northern land and gather them from the ends of the earth. \q Among them will be the blind and the lame, \q pregnant women and women in labor, all together. \q A great assembly will return here.

L.8: See, I am bringing them from the land of the north and will gather them from the farthest parts of the earth; \q among them the blind and the lame, \q the pregnant woman and she who is giving birth, together; \q a great assembly, they will return here.

R.8: I will bring them back from the land in the north. I will gather them from the ends of the earth. \q The blind and the lame will be with them, \q and women who are pregnant or about to give birth. \q A great gathering of people will come back here.

decisions.choice: the land of the north: the lands of exile, Assyria and Babylon
decisions.reason: Invaders came into Israel from the north, and the exiles were taken that way (1:14; 6:22). The promise of return from the north answers the threat (3:18; 16:15; 23:8).

decisions.choice: the blind and the lame, the pregnant and those in labor: even the weakest will come home
decisions.reason: These are the people least able to make a long journey. God's gathering leaves no one behind (Isaiah 35:5-6; 40:11; Micah 4:6-7).

decisions.choice: a great assembly: a large company gathered together
decisions.reason: The word is used of Israel gathered as a people, often for worship. The returning exiles come home as one gathered people.

decisions.choice: See (Literal); I am going to (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens with a word that calls attention to something about to happen. Balanced puts that into the verb; Readable says simply "I will".

records.source: בִּבְכִ֣י יָבֹ֗אוּ וּֽבְתַחֲנוּנִים֮ אֽוֹבִילֵם֒ אֽוֹלִיכֵם֙ אֶל־נַ֣חֲלֵי מַ֔יִם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָשָׁ֔ר לֹ֥א יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ בָּ֑הּ כִּֽי־הָיִ֤יתִי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאָ֔ב וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא׃ס
records.gloss: With weeping they will come, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them; I will make them walk to streams of water, in a straight way, [in which] they will not stumble in it; for I have become to Israel a father, and Ephraim, my firstborn [is] he.
pieces: They will come weeping, \q and I will lead them as they plead for mercy. \q I will guide them beside streams of water, \q on a level road where they will not stumble, \q because I am a father to Israel, \q and Ephraim is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} firstborn son.

L.9: With weeping they will come, \q and with pleas for mercy I will lead them; \q I will make them walk by streams of water, \q on a straight path on which they will not stumble; \q for I have become a father to Israel, \q and Ephraim is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} firstborn.

R.9: They will come back crying, \q praying for mercy as I lead them home. \q I will guide them beside streams of water, \q on a smooth road where they will not trip. \q I am a father to Israel, \q and Ephraim is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} firstborn son.

decisions.choice: weeping and pleas for mercy: the tears and prayers of people who turn back to God
decisions.reason: The weeping is probably grief over sin turning to prayer, as in Ephraim's words in verses 18-19 and in 3:21 and 50:4. It may include tears of joy at the return.

decisions.choice: streams of water, a straight path: the journey home as a new exodus
decisions.reason: God will lead the exiles as he led Israel through the desert, with water and an easy road (Isaiah 35:6-8; 40:3-4; 49:10).

decisions.choice: I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn: God's love for the people as his own son
decisions.reason: God called Israel his firstborn son at the exodus (Exodus 4:22). Ephraim, the younger son of Joseph, received the firstborn's blessing from Jacob (Genesis 48:14-20), and his name stands for the northern tribes. The firstborn had the place of honor and the double share; the north, long cast off, is restored to that place.

decisions.choice: firstborn son (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "son" so that "firstborn" is not read as a bare adjective; the picture of father and son is in the Hebrew.

records.source: שִׁמְע֤וּ דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְהַגִּ֥ידוּ בָאִיִּ֖ים מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק וְאִמְר֗וּ מְזָרֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְקַבְּצֶ֔נּוּ וּשְׁמָר֖וֹ כְּרֹעֶ֥ה עֶדְרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Hear [the] word of Yahweh, nations, and declare [it] in the coastlands from afar, and say: [He who] scatters Israel will gather him, and will keep him as a shepherd [keeps] his flock.
pieces: Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you nations; \q announce it in the coastlands far away. \q Say, "The one who scattered Israel will gather him \q and watch over him as a shepherd watches his flock."

L.10: Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, nations, \q and declare [it] in the coastlands far away; \q and say, "He who scattered Israel will gather him \q and will keep him as a shepherd [keeps] his flock."

R.10: Listen to the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you nations. \q Tell it in lands far away. \q Say, "The God who scattered Israel will gather the people again. \q He will take care of them as a shepherd takes care of his sheep."

decisions.choice: he who scattered Israel will gather him: the same God who sent the exile ends it
decisions.reason: The exile was God's own act of judgment (9:15; 13:24), so the nations are to know that he alone can undo it. The scattering and the gathering come from one hand.

decisions.choice: the coastlands: distant lands along the sea
decisions.reason: The word means coasts and islands of the Mediterranean, and so the farthest lands people knew (2:10; Isaiah 41:1). Even they are to hear of Israel's return.

decisions.choice: as a shepherd keeps his flock: God as Israel's shepherd
decisions.reason: God promised to gather the scattered flock himself after the shepherds failed it (23:1-4; Ezekiel 34:11-16; Isaiah 40:11).

decisions.choice: The God who ... the people ... them
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who scattered and turns "him" (Israel) into "the people" and "them", since the Hebrew uses one pronoun for the whole nation.

decisions.choice: coastlands (Literal, Balanced); lands far away (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah.

records.source: כִּֽי־פָדָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֑ב וּגְאָל֕וֹ מִיַּ֖ד חָזָ֥ק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: For Yahweh has ransomed Jacob, and redeemed him from [the] hand of [one] stronger than he.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has ransomed Jacob \q and redeemed him from the power of one too strong for him.

L.11: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has ransomed Jacob \q and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has paid the price to set the people of Jacob free. \q He has bought them back from an enemy that was too strong for them.

decisions.choice: ransomed, redeemed: set free by paying the price, as a near relative would
decisions.reason: The first verb means to buy someone free (Exodus 13:13; Deuteronomy 7:8). The second is the duty of the next of kin, who buys back a relative's land or freedom (Leviticus 25:25, 48-49). God acts as Israel's kinsman, as at the exodus (Exodus 6:6).

decisions.choice: has ransomed: the rescue spoken of as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the past, though the return is still to come. The prophet speaks of it as if it has happened, because God has settled it.

decisions.choice: from the hand of one stronger than he: from the power of an enemy Israel could not defeat
decisions.reason: "Hand" means power. The stronger one is the empire that held Israel captive.

decisions.choice: paid the price to set ... free ... bought them back
decisions.reason: Readable explains both verbs. "Bought back" for the next of kin's verb follows Isaiah.

records.source: וּבָאוּ֮ וְרִנְּנ֣וּ בִמְרוֹם־צִיּוֹן֒ וְנָהֲר֞וּ אֶל־ט֣וּב יְהוָ֗ה עַל־דָּגָן֙ וְעַל־תִּירֹ֣שׁ וְעַל־יִצְהָ֔ר וְעַל־בְּנֵי־צֹ֖אן וּבָקָ֑ר וְהָיְתָ֤ה נַפְשָׁם֙ כְּגַ֣ן רָוֶ֔ה וְלֹא־יוֹסִ֥יפוּ לְדַאֲבָ֖ה עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And they will come and shout for joy on [the] height of Zion, and they will be radiant over [the] goodness of Yahweh, over grain and over new wine and over fresh oil, and over [the] young of [the] flock and [the] herd; and their soul will be like a watered garden, and they will not again languish anymore.
pieces: They will come and sing out with joy on Zion's heights; \q their faces will shine over the good gifts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, over grain, new wine and oil, \q and over the young of the flocks and herds. \q Their whole life will be like a watered garden, \q and they will never grow faint again.

L.12: And they will come and shout for joy on the height of Zion, \q and they will be radiant over the goodness of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, over grain and over new wine and over oil, \q and over the young of the flock and the herd; \q and their soul will be like a watered garden, \q and they will not languish again anymore.

R.12: They will come and sing for joy on Mount Zion. \q Their faces will shine because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is so good to them. He gives them grain, new wine and olive oil, \q young sheep and young cattle. \q They will be like a garden with plenty of water, \q and they will never be weak again.

decisions.choice: be radiant: their faces will shine with joy
alternatives: they will stream to the goodness of the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to shine (Psalm 34:6; Isaiah 60:5). A verb with the same letters means to flow or stream, and some take it here as the people streaming to the LORD's good gifts, as the nations stream to Zion (Isaiah 2:2). Shining faces fit the shouts of joy in the same line.

decisions.choice: the goodness of the LORD: the good things God gives, named in the list that follows
decisions.reason: Here goodness means God's gifts: the harvest of grain, grapes and olives, and the young of the flocks and herds, the produce promised for obedience (Deuteronomy 7:13).

decisions.choice: their soul like a watered garden: their whole life refreshed and fruitful
decisions.reason: "Soul" means the person's life and inner self. A watered garden never dries up (Isaiah 58:11). Verse 25 returns to the same picture.

decisions.choice: Their faces will shine because the LORD is so good to them. He gives them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "radiant" and turns the list of the LORD's good gifts into a sentence of its own.

records.source: אָ֣ז תִּשְׂמַ֤ח בְּתוּלָה֙ בְּמָח֔וֹל וּבַחֻרִ֥ים וּזְקֵנִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וְהָפַכְתִּ֨י אֶבְלָ֤ם לְשָׂשׂוֹן֙ וְנִ֣חַמְתִּ֔ים וְשִׂמַּחְתִּ֖ים מִיגוֹנָֽם׃
records.gloss: Then will rejoice [the] virgin in [the] dance, and young men and old [men] together; and I will turn their mourning into joy, and I will comfort them and make them glad from their sorrow.
pieces: Then the young women will rejoice in the dance, \q the young men and the old men with them. \q I will turn their mourning into joy; \q I will comfort them and make them glad after their sorrow.

L.13: Then the virgin will rejoice in the dance, \q and young men and old together; \q and I will turn their mourning into joy, \q and I will comfort them and make them glad [after] their sorrow.

R.13: Then the girls will celebrate with dancing, \q and the young men and old men will join in. \q I will change their sadness into joy. \q I will comfort them and make them happy after all their sorrow.

decisions.choice: the virgin: young women as a group
decisions.reason: The word is singular, "the virgin", but here it stands for the young women of the people, set beside the young men and the old men. It is not the title "virgin Israel" of verse 4.

decisions.choice: I will turn their mourning into joy: God reverses the grief of the exile
decisions.reason: The verse answers the laments of the destruction, when joy and the sound of celebration were silenced (7:34; 16:9; 25:10). God himself makes the change (Psalm 30:12).

decisions.choice: glad from their sorrow: gladness that comes after and in place of sorrow
decisions.reason: The small word "from" can mean "after" or "instead of"; both describe sorrow giving way to joy.

decisions.choice: the young women (Balanced); the girls (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the collective singular plural.

records.source: וְרִוֵּיתִ֛י נֶ֥פֶשׁ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים דָּ֑שֶׁן וְעַמִּ֛י אֶת־טוּבִ֥י יִשְׂבָּ֖עוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will saturate [the] soul of the priests [with] fatness, and my people [with] my goodness will be satisfied, declares Yahweh.
pieces: I will fill the priests with rich food in abundance, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will have their fill of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} good gifts, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: And I will saturate the soul of the priests [with] fatness, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be satisfied with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} goodness, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: I will give the priests more than enough of the best food, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be filled with the good things I give them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: fatness: the rich portions of the sacrifices that fed the priests
decisions.reason: The priests lived on their share of the offerings (Leviticus 7:31-36; Deuteronomy 18:1-3). If they have plenty, the people are bringing many sacrifices, and worship at the temple is restored.

decisions.choice: saturate the soul: satisfy the appetite fully
decisions.reason: The verb means to give plenty to drink, to drench. "Soul" here is the appetite or the person who longs to be filled (Psalm 107:9). The same verb returns in verse 25.

decisions.choice: my goodness: the good things God gives
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "goodness" means God's gifts of food and plenty.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (Literal, Balanced); says the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, each level keeps one wording for this formula.

records.source: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה ק֣וֹל בְּרָמָ֤ה נִשְׁמָע֙ נְהִי֙ בְּכִ֣י תַמְרוּרִ֔ים רָחֵ֖ל מְבַכָּ֣ה עַל־בָּנֶ֑יהָ מֵאֲנָ֛ה לְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־בָּנֶ֖יהָ כִּ֥י אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: A voice in Ramah is heard, lamentation, weeping of bitterness; Rachel weeping over her children; she refuses to be comforted over her children, because he is not.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: In Ramah a voice is heard, mourning and bitter weeping: \q Rachel weeping for her children. \q She will not let anyone comfort her for her children, because they are gone.

L.15: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation [and] bitter weeping; \q Rachel is weeping over her children; \q she refuses to be comforted over her children, because they are not.

R.15: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: People hear a sound in Ramah, the sound of crying and bitter sadness. \q Rachel is crying for her children. \q She will not let anyone comfort her, because her children are gone.

decisions.choice: Ramah: a town of Benjamin a few miles north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Ramah lay on the road north out of Jerusalem. Jeremiah himself was set free there from among the captives being taken to Babylon (40:1), so it was a place where exiles were gathered. Rachel's tomb was remembered as being in the territory of Benjamin (1 Samuel 10:2), not far away.

decisions.choice: Rachel weeping for her children: Israel's ancestor mother grieving over her descendants taken away
decisions.reason: Rachel was Jacob's beloved wife, the mother of Joseph (father of Ephraim and Manasseh) and of Benjamin; she died giving birth to Benjamin (Genesis 35:16-20). The poem pictures her crying from her grave as her descendants, the northern tribes and Benjamin, are led into exile.

decisions.choice: because they are not: her children are gone, taken away or dead
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "because he is not", using the singular for the children as one group. "Is not" means no longer present (Genesis 37:30; 42:36). Verses 16-17 answer it: they will return.

decisions.choice: used in the New Testament: Matthew 2:18
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes this verse when Herod kills the young boys of Bethlehem, seeing in Rachel's weeping a picture of the mothers' grief (Matthew 2:16-18). In Jeremiah the lament is followed at once by the promise that her children will come home.

decisions.choice: She will not let anyone comfort her (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "refuses to be comforted" means that she turns away all comfort; Balanced and Readable say so actively.

records.heading: Rachel weeping for her children

records.source: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה מִנְעִ֤י קוֹלֵךְ֙ מִבֶּ֔כִי וְעֵינַ֖יִךְ מִדִּמְעָ֑ה כִּי֩ יֵ֨שׁ שָׂכָ֤ר לִפְעֻלָּתֵךְ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְשָׁ֖בוּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ אוֹיֵֽב׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: Restrain your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work, declares Yahweh, and they will return from [the] land of [the] enemy.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Hold back your voice from weeping \q and your eyes from tears, \q for your labor will have its reward, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q they will come back from the land of the enemy.

L.16: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Restrain your voice from weeping \q and your eyes from tears, \q for there is a reward for your work, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and they will return from the land of the enemy.

R.16: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Stop crying. \q Wipe the tears from your eyes. \q What you have done will be rewarded, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Your children will come back from the enemy's land.

decisions.choice: a reward for your work: Rachel's labor as a mother will not be wasted
decisions.reason: Her work is bearing and raising children. Since her children will come back, her labor has its reward (compare Isaiah 49:4; 65:23).

decisions.choice: they will return: Rachel's children, the exiles
decisions.reason: "They" are the children she weeps for in verse 15.

decisions.choice: Your children
decisions.reason: Readable names who will return.

records.source: וְיֵשׁ־תִּקְוָ֥ה לְאַחֲרִיתֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁ֥בוּ בָנִ֖ים לִגְבוּלָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And there is hope for your future, declares Yahweh, and children will return to their territory.
pieces: There is hope for your future, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q your children will come back to their own land.

L.17: And there is hope for your future, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and children will return to their own territory.

R.17: There is hope for you in the days ahead, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Your children will come back to their own land.

decisions.choice: your future: what lies ahead for you, including descendants
decisions.reason: The word means the end or latter part of something, and so the future (29:11). Rachel's future is her children and their children.

decisions.choice: their own territory: the land of their tribes
decisions.reason: The word means a border, and so the land within it. The exiles will go back to their own tribal land.

decisions.choice: your children
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "children"; Balanced and Readable add "your", since they are Rachel's children of verse 15.

records.source: שָׁמ֣וֹעַ שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ מִתְנוֹדֵ֔ד יִסַּרְתַּ֨נִי֙ וָֽאִוָּסֵ֔ר כְּעֵ֖גֶל לֹ֣א לֻמָּ֑ד הֲשִׁיבֵ֣נִי וְאָשׁ֔וּבָה כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: Surely I have heard Ephraim bemoaning himself: You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like a calf [that was] not trained; bring me back, and I will return, for you [are] Yahweh my God.
pieces: I have certainly heard Ephraim grieving: \q "You disciplined me, and I took the discipline, \q like a calf never trained to the yoke. \q Bring me back, and I will come back, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.

L.18: I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: \q "You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, \q like a calf not trained; \q bring me back, and I will come back, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.

R.18: I have clearly heard Ephraim crying: \q "You corrected me, and I was corrected, \q like a young calf that had never been trained. \q Bring me back, and I will come back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.

decisions.choice: I have surely heard Ephraim: God speaks, and Ephraim's own prayer follows to the end of verse 19
decisions.reason: The doubled verb stresses that God has truly heard. Ephraim, the leading tribe of the north, stands for the northern people (verse 9). The verb for grieving means to shake the head or rock to and fro in sorrow.

decisions.choice: like a calf not trained: a young animal that resisted the yoke until it was broken in
decisions.reason: Hosea pictures Ephraim as a stubborn heifer (Hosea 4:16; 10:11). The discipline was the suffering of defeat and exile; Ephraim now accepts that it was needed.

decisions.choice: bring me back, and I will come back: both the journey home and the return to God
alternatives: turn me, and I will turn (repentance only)
decisions.reason: The verb is the same one used for repentance and for coming home from exile. Ephraim asks God to make him turn and confesses that he cannot turn on his own (compare Lamentations 5:21).

decisions.choice: Quotation marks for Ephraim's words
decisions.reason: Ephraim's prayer is speech quoted inside God's oracle, so it takes double quotation marks, opening here and closing at the end of verse 19. Its opening "You" begins a sentence and is capitalized at every setting.

decisions.choice: come back to you
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to you" to make plain that the return is to God.

records.source: כִּֽי־אַחֲרֵ֤י שׁוּבִי֙ נִחַ֔מְתִּי וְאַֽחֲרֵי֙ הִוָּ֣דְעִ֔י סָפַ֖קְתִּי עַל־יָרֵ֑ךְ בֹּ֚שְׁתִּי וְגַם־נִכְלַ֔מְתִּי כִּ֥י נָשָׂ֖אתִי חֶרְפַּ֥ת נְעוּרָֽי׃
records.gloss: For after my turning away I repented, and after I was made to know, I struck on [my] thigh; I was ashamed and also humiliated, because I bore [the] disgrace of my youth.
pieces: After I turned away, I was sorry; \q after I came to understand, I struck my thigh in grief. \q I was ashamed and disgraced, \q because I carried the shame of my youth."

L.19: For after my turning away I repented, \q and after I was made to understand I struck [my] thigh; \q I was ashamed and also humiliated, \q for I bore the disgrace of my youth."

R.19: After I turned away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I was sorry. \q When I understood what I had done, I struck my thigh in grief. \q I was ashamed and felt disgraced, \q because I still carried the disgrace of the sins I did when I was young."

decisions.choice: after my turning away: after Ephraim turned from God
alternatives: after I turned back, I repented
decisions.reason: The word "turning" can mean turning away from God or turning back to him. With "I repented" following, it most likely means that after Ephraim had turned away, it came to regret it. Others read "after I turned back (to you), I repented", that is, sorrow followed the return.

decisions.choice: struck my thigh: a gesture of grief and dismay
decisions.reason: Slapping the thigh showed great sorrow or alarm (Ezekiel 21:17).

decisions.choice: the disgrace of my youth: the shame of the sins of Israel's early days
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom's "youth" is its early history, when it turned to other gods (3:24-25; compare Psalm 25:7). Ephraim feels the shame of that past.

decisions.choice: in grief
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the gesture meant.

decisions.choice: from you ... the sins I did when I was young
decisions.reason: Readable says from whom Ephraim turned and explains the disgrace of youth. Ephraim's words close here.

records.source: הֲבֵן֩ יַקִּ֨יר לִ֜י אֶפְרַ֗יִם אִ֚ם יֶ֣לֶד שַׁעֲשֻׁעִ֔ים כִּֽי־מִדֵּ֤י דַבְּרִי֙ בּ֔וֹ זָכֹ֥ר אֶזְכְּרֶ֖נּוּ ע֑וֹד עַל־כֵּ֗ן הָמ֤וּ מֵעַי֙ ל֔וֹ רַחֵ֥ם אֲֽרַחֲמֶ֖נּוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: [Is] a son dear to me Ephraim, or a child of delights? For as often as I speak against him, I surely remember him still; therefore my inner parts are stirred for him; I will surely have compassion on him, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Is Ephraim {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear son, a child who delights {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q For whenever I speak against him, \q I still remember him and cannot forget. \q That is why {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart aches for him; \q I will surely show him compassion, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.20: Is Ephraim a dear son to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, or a child of delight? \q For as often as I speak against him, \q I surely remember him still; \q therefore {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inner parts are stirred for him; \q I will surely have compassion on him, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: Is Ephraim not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear son, the child I love? \q Even when I speak against him, \q I still think of him. \q That is why {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart longs for him. \q I will surely show him mercy, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Is Ephraim a dear son to me?: a question expecting the answer yes
alternatives: a question of wonder or surprise
decisions.reason: God answers Ephraim's prayer with a question that confesses his love: Ephraim is his precious child. Some read it as a question of wonder ("Is Ephraim really so dear to me, that ...?"), but the rest of the verse shows that the answer is yes.

decisions.choice: as often as I speak against him, I still remember him: even God's words of judgment do not end his love
decisions.reason: God has spoken against Ephraim many times through the prophets, yet the doubled verb stresses that he keeps remembering him with care.

decisions.choice: my inner parts are stirred: I am deeply moved
decisions.reason: The inner parts (the belly or bowels) were thought of as the seat of strong feeling (Isaiah 16:11; 63:15). The verb means to be in turmoil, to groan.

decisions.choice: have compassion: a love like a mother's for her child
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for womb. It echoes Rachel weeping for her children (verse 15): God's love for Ephraim is like a mother's.

decisions.choice: my heart (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "heart" for the inner parts, where English places such feelings.

decisions.choice: Is Ephraim not my dear son
decisions.reason: Readable adds "not" to show that the question expects the answer yes.

records.source: הַצִּ֧יבִי לָ֣ךְ צִיֻּנִ֗ים שִׂ֤מִי לָךְ֙ תַּמְרוּרִ֔ים שִׁ֣תִי לִבֵּ֔ךְ לַֽמְסִלָּ֖ה דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָלָ֑כְתְּ שׁ֚וּבִי בְּתוּלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֻׁ֖בִי אֶל־עָרַ֥יִךְ אֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: Set up for yourself road markers, place for yourself guideposts; set your heart to the highway, [the] way [that] you went; return, virgin of Israel, return to these your cities.
pieces: Set up road markers for yourself; \q put up signposts. \q Fix your mind on the highway, the road you traveled. \q Come back, Virgin Israel; \q come back to these towns of yours.

L.21: Set up road markers for yourself; \q make guideposts for yourself; \q set your heart toward the highway, the road [by which] you went. \q Return, virgin Israel; \q return to these your cities.

R.21: Put up signs along the road. \q Set up markers to show the way. \q Remember the road you took when you went away. \q Come back, people of Israel, pure as a young woman. \q Come back to these towns of yours.

decisions.choice: you went: the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters can be read "I went"; the scribes' marginal note (qere) reads "you went", which suits the woman addressed throughout the verse. The translation follows the marginal reading.

decisions.choice: road markers, guideposts: stones or posts set up to mark the way
decisions.reason: The exiles are to mark the road as they leave, so that they can find it again on the way home. The word for guideposts sounds the same as "bitter" in verse 15: the road of bitter tears becomes the road home.

decisions.choice: set your heart: pay close attention, keep in mind
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will.

decisions.choice: Come back (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb that means both turning back to God and coming home is "return" at Literal and "come back" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 18.

records.source: עַד־מָתַי֙ תִּתְחַמָּקִ֔ין הַבַּ֖ת הַשּֽׁוֹבֵבָ֑ה כִּֽי־בָרָ֨א יְהוָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ נְקֵבָ֖ה תְּס֥וֹבֵֽב גָּֽבֶר׃ס
records.gloss: Until when will you turn this way and that, the daughter, the faithless one? For Yahweh has created a new [thing] in the land: a female will surround a man.
pieces: How long will you waver this way and that, \q you faithless daughter? \q For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has created something new in the land: \q a woman will encircle a man.

L.22: How long will you turn this way and that, \q faithless daughter? \q For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has created a new thing in the land: \q a female will surround a man.

R.22: How long will you keep wandering here and there, \q you unfaithful daughter? \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made something new happen in the land: \q a woman will surround a man.

decisions.choice: turn this way and that, faithless daughter: Israel hesitating to come home
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn about, to waver. "Faithless" comes from the same root as "return" in verse 21, a play on words heard also in 3:14, 22: the daughter who turns away is called to turn back.

decisions.choice: the LORD has created a new thing: something only God can bring about
decisions.reason: The verb for create is used only of God (Genesis 1:1; Isaiah 43:19; 65:17). The new thing gives the hesitant daughter a reason to come home.

decisions.choice: a female will surround a man: a saying whose meaning is very uncertain
alternatives: a woman will protect a man
a woman will court (or embrace) a man
decisions.reason: The words are clear, but their sense is not. Readings offered include: the woman (Israel) will embrace or seek her husband (God), reversing her running away; the weak will protect the strong, as a woman guarding a warrior, so that Israel will be safe; or a woman will court a man, a sign of a world turned upside down by joy. Some early Christian readers saw in it the virgin birth. The text itself does not settle it, and the translation keeps the bare words.

decisions.choice: in the land: in Israel's own land, or on the earth
decisions.reason: The word can mean the earth or the land. The call to return to "these your cities" (verse 21) favors the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: you unfaithful daughter
decisions.reason: Readable says "unfaithful" for faithless, a more common word.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ע֣וֹד יֹאמְר֞וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבְעָרָ֔יו בְּשׁוּבִ֖י אֶת־שְׁבוּתָ֑ם יְבָרֶכְךָ֧ יְהוָ֛ה נְוֵה־צֶ֖דֶק הַ֥ר הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Again they will say the word the this in [the] land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: May Yahweh bless you, abode of righteousness, mountain of holiness.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: When I restore their fortunes, people in the land of Judah and in its towns will once again use these words: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, home of righteousness, holy mountain!"

L.23: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Once again they will say this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, abode of righteousness, mountain of holiness."

R.23: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: When I make things good again for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, those who live in the land of Judah and its towns will say once more, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, holy mountain, home where righteousness lives!"

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes: bring the people back from exile and make them prosper
decisions.reason: The phrase means to turn things back to how they were, and in Jeremiah it often includes the return of the captives (29:14; 30:3, 18).

decisions.choice: abode of righteousness, mountain of holiness: Jerusalem and the temple mount
decisions.reason: The first word means a pasture or a settled home. The blessing is spoken over Zion, the holy hill where God lives (Psalm 2:6; Isaiah 1:26). In 50:7 the LORD himself is called the "abode of righteousness" of Israel's ancestors.

decisions.choice: prose from here to the end of the chapter
decisions.reason: From this verse on, the chapter is set as prose. Verses 23-26 still have parallel lines, and so do verses 35-37, but they are joined to the prose promises of verses 27-40 and set the same way.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: people ... those who live
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "they will say" has no named subject; Balanced and Readable supply one. Readable also explains "restore their fortunes".

records.source: וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ בָ֛הּ יְהוּדָ֥ה וְכָל־עָרָ֖יו יַחְדָּ֑ו אִכָּרִ֕ים וְנָסְע֖וּ בַּעֵֽדֶר׃
records.gloss: And will dwell in it Judah and all its cities together, farmers, and they journey with [the] flock.
pieces: Judah and all its towns will live there together, the farmers and those who move about with the flocks.

L.24: And Judah and all its cities will dwell in it together, farmers and [those who] travel with the flock.

R.24: The people of Judah and of all its towns will live there together. Farmers will live there, and so will shepherds who move from place to place with their sheep.

decisions.choice: in it: in the land of Judah
decisions.reason: "It" refers back to the land of Judah of verse 23.

decisions.choice: farmers and those who travel with the flock: both settled and roaming ways of life
decisions.reason: Farmers stayed with their fields; shepherds moved from pasture to pasture. Both can live safely in the land again, with no enemy to fear (contrast 6:3; 33:12-13).

decisions.choice: shepherds who move from place to place
decisions.reason: Readable says who those traveling with the flocks are.

records.source: כִּ֥י הִרְוֵ֖יתִי נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וְכָל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ דָּאֲבָ֖ה מִלֵּֽאתִי׃
records.gloss: For I give drink [to the] weary soul, and every languishing soul I fill.
pieces: For I refresh the weary soul and satisfy everyone who is faint.

L.25: For I give drink to the weary soul, and every languishing soul I fill.

R.25: I give new strength to those who are tired, and I satisfy all who are weak.

decisions.choice: I give drink ... I fill: God's settled purpose, spoken of as already done
alternatives: I have refreshed ... I have filled
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the past form, used here for what God has firmly decided to do. They pick up verses 12 and 14: the soul like a watered garden, the priests' soul filled.

decisions.choice: the weary soul, every languishing soul: people worn out by the suffering of war and exile
decisions.reason: "Soul" means the whole person, here as thirsty and faint. The word for languishing is the one in verse 12: "they will not languish again".

decisions.choice: give new strength
decisions.reason: Readable says what giving drink to the weary means.

records.source: עַל־זֹ֖את הֱקִיצֹ֣תִי וָאֶרְאֶ֑ה וּשְׁנָתִ֖י עָ֥רְבָה לִּֽי׃ס
records.gloss: On this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant to me.
pieces: At this I woke up and looked around, and my sleep had been sweet to me.

L.26: At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant to me.

R.26: Then I woke up and looked around. My sleep had been pleasant.

decisions.choice: I awoke: the prophet speaks, waking from a revelation given in sleep
decisions.reason: The speaker is most likely Jeremiah. The promises of verses 2-25 (or at least 23-25) came to him as in a dream, and he wakes refreshed by them. The verse is very unusual in Jeremiah, and some take it as the words of the exiles, or of God rising to act (Psalm 78:65).

decisions.choice: my sleep was pleasant: the vision gave peace
decisions.reason: Unlike troubling dreams (Daniel 2:1), this one left the sleeper glad.

decisions.choice: looked around
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "around" to make clear that the prophet, now awake, looks at what is about him.

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְזָרַעְתִּ֗י אֶת־בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה זֶ֥רַע אָדָ֖ם וְזֶ֥רַע בְּהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, when I will sow [the] house of Israel and [the] house of Judah [with] seed of man and seed of beast.
pieces: The days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will sow seed in the house of Israel and the house of Judah, the seed of people and the seed of animals.

L.27: Look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah [with] seed of {{gender:humankind|man}} and seed of beast.

R.27: A time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will fill Israel and Judah with people and animals, as a farmer sows a field with seed.

decisions.choice: sow with the seed of humans and of animals: fill the land again with people and livestock
decisions.reason: The land had been left empty of people and animals (32:43; 33:10). God will scatter new life over it like a farmer sowing seed, so that it grows full again (Hosea 2:25; Ezekiel 36:9-11).

decisions.choice: the house of Israel and the house of Judah: both kingdoms, north and south
decisions.reason: The promise again includes both parts of the divided people, as the new covenant does (verse 31).

decisions.choice: Look, days are coming (Literal); The days are coming (Balanced); A time is coming (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Jeremiah (7:32; 9:24; 16:14).

decisions.choice: as a farmer sows a field with seed
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of sowing.

records.source: וְהָיָ֞ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר שָׁקַ֣דְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לִנְת֧וֹשׁ וְלִנְת֛וֹץ וְלַהֲרֹ֖ס וּלְהַאֲבִ֣יד וּלְהָרֵ֑עַ כֵּ֣ן אֶשְׁקֹ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם לִבְנ֥וֹת וְלִנְט֖וֹעַ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be, just as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down and to overthrow and to destroy and to do harm, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Just as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, to overthrow, to destroy and to bring harm, so I will keep watch over them to build and to plant, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.28: And it will be, just as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, and to overthrow and to destroy and to bring harm, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.28: In the past I kept watch over them to uproot and tear down, to overthrow, destroy and bring harm. Now I will keep watch over them to build and plant, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, overthrow, destroy, build, plant: the words of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: These are the verbs of 1:10, where God set Jeremiah over nations "to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant". Here "overthrow" comes before "destroy", and a fifth word of judgment is added: "to bring harm". The judgment Jeremiah announced has come; now the last two words come true.

decisions.choice: watched over them: God watching over his word to carry it out
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in 1:12, "I am watching over my word to do it", the word play on the almond tree. The same care that carried out the judgment will now carry out the restoration (compare 44:27).

decisions.choice: to bring harm: to bring disaster
decisions.reason: The verb means to do evil to, in the sense of causing harm or calamity, not wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, overthrow, destroy, build, plant
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the English verbs of 1:10 for the same Hebrew verbs, so the echo can be heard. The added verb is "bring harm".

decisions.choice: In the past ... Now
decisions.reason: Readable splits the comparison into two sentences and marks the change of time.

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם לֹא־יֹאמְר֣וּ ע֔וֹד אָב֖וֹת אָ֣כְלוּ בֹ֑סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י בָנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה׃
records.gloss: In the days the those they will not say again: Fathers have eaten sour grape[s], and [the] teeth of [the] children are blunted.
pieces: In those days people will no longer say, "The {{gender:parents|fathers}} ate sour grapes, but it is the children whose teeth are set on edge."

L.29: In those days they will no longer say, "Fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are blunted."

R.29: At that time people will no longer say, "The {{gender:parents|fathers}} ate the sour grapes, but the children got the sour taste."

decisions.choice: the fathers ate sour grapes, and the children's teeth are blunted: a proverb that the children suffer for their parents' sins
decisions.reason: Unripe grapes leave a rough, dull feeling on the teeth. The proverb complained that the generation of the exile was being punished for what earlier generations had done (Lamentations 5:7; compare 2 Kings 24:3-4).

decisions.choice: the same proverb in Ezekiel 18:2
decisions.reason: Ezekiel quotes the same saying among the exiles and answers it at length: each person who sins will die for their own sin (Ezekiel 18:3-4, 20).

decisions.choice: blunted: made dull, set on edge
decisions.reason: The verb describes the dull, rough feeling of teeth after something sour.

decisions.choice: parents (with fathers as the alternative)
decisions.reason: The proverb speaks of the older generation as a whole; the gender setting gives "fathers" as the alternative. Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: set on edge (Balanced); got the sour taste (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English phrase for the feeling; Readable says it plainly.

records.source: כִּ֛י אִם־אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנ֖וֹ יָמ֑וּת כָּל־הָֽאָדָ֛ם הָאֹכֵ֥ל הַבֹּ֖סֶר תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: But each for his own iniquity will die; every man who eats the sour grape[s], his teeth will be blunted.
pieces: Instead, each will die for {{gender:their|his}} own guilt; whoever eats the sour grapes, it is {{gender:their|his}} own teeth that will be set on edge.

L.30: But each one will die for {{gender:their|his}} own iniquity; every {{gender:person|man}} who eats the sour grapes, {{gender:their|his}} teeth will be blunted.

R.30: Instead, people will die for their own sins. Whoever eats sour grapes will get the sour taste in {{gender:their|his}} own mouth.

decisions.choice: each will die for their own iniquity: everyone answers for their own sin
decisions.reason: The new age will make plain that God judges each person for their own wrong (Deuteronomy 24:16; Ezekiel 18:20). The verse does not deny that sin harms later generations; it denies that the innocent bear another's guilt before God.

decisions.choice: iniquity: wrongdoing and the guilt it brings
decisions.reason: The word covers both the wrong done and the guilt and punishment that follow.

decisions.choice: iniquity (Literal); guilt (Balanced); sins (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: their, person (with his, man as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: "Each" and "every man" here mean every person, man or woman; the gender setting gives the traditional forms.

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְכָרַתִּ֗י אֶת־בֵּ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּרִ֥ית חֲדָשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: Look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, when I will make with [the] house of Israel and with [the] house of Judah a covenant new,
pieces: The days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and then I will make a covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah: a new covenant.

L.31: Look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will make with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah a new covenant,

R.31: A time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and the people of Judah.

decisions.choice: a new covenant: a new binding relationship between God and his people
decisions.reason: A covenant is a solemn agreement that binds two parties, here God and Israel. The covenant made at Sinai had been broken (verse 32; 11:10). God promises a new one, described in verses 33-34; it is the only place in the Hebrew Scriptures where the phrase "new covenant" occurs.

decisions.choice: make a covenant: literally "cut" a covenant
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is "cut", probably from the rite of cutting animals in two when a covenant was made (34:18; Genesis 15:9-18).

decisions.choice: used in the New Testament: Hebrews 8:8-12; 10:16-17; Luke 22:20; 1 Corinthians 11:25
decisions.reason: Hebrews quotes verses 31-34 in full, and again in part, to show that the covenant made through Christ fulfills this promise. At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of the cup as "the new covenant in my blood". These are New Testament readings of the promise; in Jeremiah it is made to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

decisions.choice: the sentence continues into verse 32
decisions.reason: Verse 32 goes on to say what the new covenant will not be like.

decisions.choice: and then I will make a covenant ... a new covenant
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew order, with "new covenant" at the end of the sentence where the Hebrew puts it, and repeats "covenant" to make that order natural. "And then" gives the Hebrew "and" that joins the promise to the coming days.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel and the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of" for "the house of".

records.heading: A new covenant

records.source: לֹ֣א כַבְּרִ֗ית אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּרַ֨תִּי֙ אֶת־אֲבוֹתָ֔ם בְּיוֹם֙ הֶחֱזִיקִ֣י בְיָדָ֔ם לְהוֹצִיאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֖רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֜מָּה הֵפֵ֣רוּ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֗י וְאָנֹכִ֛י בָּעַ֥לְתִּי בָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: not like the covenant that I made with their fathers in [the] day of my taking hold of their hand to bring them out from [the] land of Egypt, which they, they broke my covenant, and I, I was husband over them, declares Yahweh.
pieces: It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors on the day I took their hand to lead them out from the land of Egypt. They broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, though I was their husband, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant that they broke, though I was a husband to them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt. They broke that covenant, even though I was like a husband to them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the covenant made with their fathers at the exodus: the covenant of Sinai
decisions.reason: God made his covenant with Israel at Mount Sinai after bringing them out of Egypt (Exodus 19:4-6; 24:3-8). Jeremiah has already charged the people with breaking it (11:3-10).

decisions.choice: took them by the hand: led them as a parent leads a child
decisions.reason: The picture is of tender guidance (Hosea 11:1-3), not force.

decisions.choice: I was a husband to them: God bound to Israel as husband, and so also as master
decisions.reason: The verb means to marry, to be a husband, and so to be lord or master over someone (3:14; Isaiah 54:5). It sets Israel's breaking of the covenant against God's faithfulness as a husband. The Greek translation, which Hebrews 8:9 quotes, reads "and I turned away from them" (or "I did not care for them"), perhaps from a Hebrew word that differs by one letter.

decisions.choice: though I was a husband: a contrast between their unfaithfulness and God's faithfulness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "they" against "I": they broke the covenant, and yet I was their husband.

decisions.choice: fathers (Literal); ancestors (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Here "fathers" means the earlier generations.

decisions.choice: like a husband
decisions.reason: Readable marks the picture as a comparison.

records.source: כִּ֣י זֹ֣את הַבְּרִ֡ית אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶכְרֹת֩ אֶת־בֵּ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אַחֲרֵ֨י הַיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵם֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה נָתַ֤תִּי אֶת־תּֽוֹרָתִי֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔ם וְעַל־לִבָּ֖ם אֶכְתֲּבֶ֑נָּה וְהָיִ֤יתִי לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ־לִ֥י לְעָֽם׃
records.gloss: For this [is] the covenant that I will make with [the] house of Israel after the days the those, declares Yahweh: I will put my instruction within them, and on their heart I will write it; and I will be to them for God, and they, they will be to me for a people.
pieces: Rather, this will be the covenant that I make with the house of Israel when those days are past, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction deep inside them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

L.33: For this [is] the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction within them, and on their heart I will write it; and I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

R.33: But this is the new covenant I will make with the people of Israel after that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching inside them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

decisions.choice: my instruction: God's teaching, the law given in the covenant
decisions.reason: The word means instruction or teaching, and is the name for the law of Moses. The new covenant does not bring a new law; it puts God's own teaching inside his people. Hebrews 8:10 has "my laws".

decisions.choice: within them, on their heart: obedience from the inside
decisions.reason: The old covenant was written on tablets of stone (Exodus 24:12; 31:18); the people's sin was written on their hearts (17:1). Now God himself will write his teaching on the heart, the seat of thought and will, so that they want to do it (24:7; 32:39-40; Ezekiel 36:26-27).

decisions.choice: I will be their God, and they will be my people: the covenant promise kept at last
decisions.reason: The aim of the covenant from the beginning (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12; Jeremiah 7:23; 31:1) is now reached.

decisions.choice: after those days: in the time to come
decisions.reason: "Those days" are the days of verse 31. The phrase points to the future, when the judgment is over.

decisions.choice: the house of Israel: the whole reunited people
decisions.reason: Only Israel is named here, but after verse 31 it means the whole people, Israel and Judah together.

decisions.choice: instruction (Literal, Balanced); teaching (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: the new covenant
decisions.reason: Readable adds "new" to link back to verse 31.

records.source: וְלֹ֧א יְלַמְּד֣וּ ע֗וֹד אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֜הוּ וְאִ֤ישׁ אֶת־אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר דְּע֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־כוּלָּם֩ יֵדְע֨וּ אוֹתִ֜י לְמִקְטַנָּ֤ם וְעַד־גְּדוֹלָם֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֤י אֶסְלַח֙ לַֽעֲוֺנָ֔ם וּלְחַטָּאתָ֖ם לֹ֥א אֶזְכָּר־עֽוֹד׃ס
records.gloss: And they will not teach again, each his neighbor and each his brother, saying, Know Yahweh; for they all will know me, from their least and to their greatest, declares Yahweh; for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will not remember again.
pieces: No longer will each one teach {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, or each one {{gender:their|his}} {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, saying, "Know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," because all of them will know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, from the least to the greatest, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For I will forgive their guilt, and I will remember their sin no more.

L.34: And they will no longer teach, each {{gender:their|his}} neighbor and each {{gender:their|his}} {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, saying, "Know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," for they will all know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, from the least of them to the greatest of them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more.

R.34: They will not need to teach their neighbors or their relatives to know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because all of them will know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, from the least important to the most important, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will forgive their sins and never again remember the wrong they have done.

decisions.choice: know the LORD: know God personally, in a living relationship of trust and obedience
decisions.reason: To know God is more than knowing about him; it means doing justice and living close to him (9:23; 22:15-16; Hosea 6:6). In the new covenant every member of the people will know God, not only priests and prophets.

decisions.choice: from the least to the greatest: everyone, whatever their age or rank
decisions.reason: The phrase means all without exception (6:13; 42:1).

decisions.choice: for I will forgive: forgiveness is the ground of the new covenant
decisions.reason: The "for" gives the reason: all will know God because he forgives. "Remember no more" means that God will no longer hold the sin against them; it does not mean that he forgets (compare Isaiah 43:25).

decisions.choice: used in the New Testament: Hebrews 8:11-12; 10:17
decisions.reason: Hebrews quotes the promise of forgiveness to show that no further offering for sin is needed (Hebrews 10:17-18).

decisions.choice: their neighbor, their brother or sister (with his neighbor, his brother as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "each his neighbor and each his brother" means everyone in the community, women and men. Readable says "relatives" for the family word, which needs no span.

decisions.choice: iniquity, sin (Literal); guilt, sin (Balanced); sins, the wrong they have done (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced says "guilt" and Readable "sins" for the first word; Readable gives the second as "the wrong they have done".

decisions.choice: They will not need to teach
decisions.reason: Readable adds "need" to show that the teaching stops because it is no longer necessary.

records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh, [who] gives [the] sun for light by day, [the] fixed orders of [the] moon and stars for light [by] night, [who] stirs up the sea, and its waves roar, Yahweh of hosts [is] his name:
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who gives the sun to light the day and the moon and stars in their fixed order to light the night, who stirs up the sea until its waves roar; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name:

L.35: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who gives the sun for light by day, the fixed orders of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name:

R.35: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. He gives the sun to shine during the day. He set the moon and stars in their order to shine at night. He stirs up the sea and makes its waves roar. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. He says:

decisions.choice: the fixed orders: the laws God set for the moon and stars
decisions.reason: The word means decrees or statutes. Here it is the order God gave to the heavens, so that they keep their courses (Genesis 1:14-18; 8:22; Job 38:33). The same word is used in verse 36 and in 33:25.

decisions.choice: stirs up the sea: churns the sea into a storm
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to stir up or to calm, but the roaring waves favor "stir up". Isaiah 51:15 has the same line.

decisions.choice: the same words as Isaiah 51:15
decisions.reason: "Who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar; the LORD of hosts is his name" is word for word the line of Isaiah 51:15, and the wording here follows it.

decisions.choice: He gives ... He set ... He stirs up ... He says:
decisions.reason: Readable turns the descriptions of God into short sentences and adds "He says" before the promise of verse 36.

records.source: אִם־יָמֻ֜שׁוּ הַחֻקִּ֥ים הָאֵ֛לֶּה מִלְּפָנַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה גַּם֩ זֶ֨רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל יִשְׁבְּת֗וּ מִֽהְי֥וֹת גּ֛וֹי לְפָנַ֖י כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: If these fixed orders depart from before me, declares Yahweh, also [the] offspring of Israel will cease from being a nation before me all the days.
pieces: Only if this fixed order ever failed before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, would the descendants of Israel ever cease to be a nation before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.36: If these fixed orders depart from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then the offspring of Israel also will cease from being a nation before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for all time.

R.36: Only if these laws that keep the sun, moon and stars in place stopped working, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, would the people of Israel ever stop being a nation in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight.

decisions.choice: if ... then also: an impossible condition that makes the promise certain
decisions.reason: The order of the heavens will not fail, so Israel will not cease to be God's nation. The same kind of oath appears in 33:20-21, 25-26.

decisions.choice: the offspring of Israel: the descendants of Israel, the people
decisions.reason: The word is "seed", meaning descendants (verse 27 uses it of new life sown in the land).

decisions.choice: all the days: for all time
decisions.reason: The phrase means always, forever.

decisions.choice: Only if ... would ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the impossible condition so that the certainty of the promise is clear.

decisions.choice: these laws that keep the sun, moon and stars in place
decisions.reason: Readable says what the fixed orders of verse 35 are.

records.source: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִם־יִמַּ֤דּוּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה וְיֵחָקְר֥וּ מֽוֹסְדֵי־אֶ֖רֶץ לְמָ֑טָּה גַּם־אֲנִ֞י אֶמְאַ֨ס בְּכָל־זֶ֧רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: If [the] heavens above can be measured, and [the] foundations of [the] earth below be searched out, also I will reject all [the] offspring of Israel for all that they have done, declares Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Only if someone could measure the heavens above and search out the foundations of the earth below would I reject all the descendants of Israel because of all they have done, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.37: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: If the heavens above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth below searched out, then I also will reject all the offspring of Israel for all that they have done, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.37: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: No one can measure the sky above or explore the deep foundations of the earth. Only if someone could do that would I reject the people of Israel, even for all they have done, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: if the heavens can be measured ... then I will reject: a second impossible condition
decisions.reason: No one can measure the heavens or search out the earth's foundations (Job 38:4-6; Isaiah 40:12). So God will never reject Israel as a whole.

decisions.choice: for all that they have done: God admits the people's sins would deserve rejection
decisions.reason: God does not deny that Israel's sins are great. The promise rests on his faithfulness, not on their deserving it.

decisions.choice: No one can measure ... Only if someone could do that
decisions.reason: Readable first states that the condition is impossible, then gives the promise.

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖יםנְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְנִבְנְתָ֤ה הָעִיר֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה מִמִּגְדַּ֥ל חֲנַנְאֵ֖ל שַׁ֥עַר הַפִּנָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, days [are coming], declares Yahweh, when the city will be rebuilt for Yahweh from [the] Tower of Hananel [to the] Gate of the Corner.
pieces: The days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when the city will be rebuilt for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.

L.38: Look, days [are] coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when the city will be rebuilt for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the Tower of Hananel [to] the Corner Gate.

R.38: A time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when Jerusalem will be rebuilt for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It will reach from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.

decisions.choice: are coming: the word read aloud but not written in the Hebrew text
alternatives: Look, days, declares the LORD (written text)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "Look, days, declares the LORD"; the scribes' marginal note (qere) supplies "are coming", as in verses 27 and 31. The translation follows the marginal reading.

decisions.choice: the Tower of Hananel and the Corner Gate: points on the north wall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Tower of Hananel stood at the north-east corner of the city near the Sheep Gate (Nehemiah 3:1; 12:39); the Corner Gate was at the north-west (2 Kings 14:13; Zechariah 14:10). Their exact places are uncertain. The line runs along the whole north side.

decisions.choice: rebuilt for the LORD: a city belonging to God
decisions.reason: The city will be built as God's own, and verse 40 calls it holy to the LORD.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem ... It will reach
decisions.reason: Readable names the city and says that the two places mark its extent.

records.gloss: And will go out again [the] measuring line straight ahead over [the] hill of Gareb, and it will turn [to] Goah.
pieces: The measuring line will stretch out farther, straight to the hill of Gareb, and then turn toward Goah.

L.39: And the measuring line will go out again, straight ahead to the hill of Gareb, and it will turn to Goah.

R.39: The measuring line will go on from there straight to the hill of Gareb and then turn toward Goah.

decisions.choice: the measuring line: the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a slightly different spelling of the word for line; the marginal note (qere) gives the usual form. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: Gareb and Goah: places on the west or south of the city, otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: These names occur nowhere else in Scripture, and where they were is not known. The line of verses 38-40 seems to run around the city from the north, west and south to the Kidron in the east.

decisions.choice: the measuring line: a cord used to mark out a building plot
decisions.reason: Builders and surveyors marked out land with a line (Zechariah 2:5-6; Ezekiel 40:3). Here it marks out the new city, larger than before.

records.source: וְכָל־הָעֵ֣מֶק הַפְּגָרִ֣ים׀וְהַדֶּ֡שֶׁן וְכָֽל־הַשְּׁדֵמוֹת֩ עַד־נַ֨חַל קִדְר֜וֹן עַד־פִּנַּ֨ת שַׁ֤עַר הַסּוּסִים֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יִנָּתֵ֧שׁ וְֽלֹא־יֵהָרֵ֛ס ע֖וֹד לְעוֹלָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And all the valley of the corpses and the fat ashes, and all the fields to [the] Wadi Kidron, to [the] corner of [the] Gate of the Horses toward [the] east, [will be] holy to Yahweh; it will not be uprooted, and it will not be overthrown again forever.
pieces: The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the fields out to the Kidron Valley, as far as the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Never again will it be uprooted or overthrown.

L.40: And the whole valley of the corpses and the ashes, and all the fields as far as the Wadi Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, [will be] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it will not be uprooted, and it will not be overthrown again, forever.

R.40: The whole valley where dead bodies and ashes were thrown, and all the fields as far as the Kidron Valley, east to the corner of the Horse Gate, will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a holy place. The city will never again be uprooted or overthrown.

decisions.choice: the valley of the corpses and the ashes: probably the Valley of Ben-hinnom, south of the city
decisions.reason: Jeremiah said that this valley, where children were sacrificed, would be filled with the dead (7:31-33; 19:6). The ashes are the fatty ashes of burnt sacrifices (Leviticus 1:16; 4:12). The most unclean place around the city will become holy.

decisions.choice: the fields: the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a word that looks similar but is otherwise unknown; the marginal note (qere) gives the word for fields or terraces (Deuteronomy 32:32; Isaiah 16:8). The translation follows the marginal reading.

decisions.choice: the Wadi Kidron and the Horse Gate: the eastern side of the city
decisions.reason: The Kidron is the valley east of Jerusalem, below the temple. The Horse Gate was in the east wall near the temple (Nehemiah 3:28; 2 Kings 11:16).

decisions.choice: not uprooted, not overthrown: the words of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: The verbs are those of 1:10 and verse 28. The judgment they announced will never come again on the rebuilt city.

decisions.choice: uprooted, overthrown
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the verbs of 1:10.

decisions.choice: will belong to the LORD as a holy place ... The city
decisions.reason: Readable explains "holy to the LORD" and names the city as what will not be uprooted.
